Hi Tom / Jenna,

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. As discussed, I'm drafting the mutual action plan (MAP) milestone for the load/performance test so we can align on responsibilities and target dates. Summary below — please review and flag anything missing: 

MAP milestone: Load / Performance Test (traffic replay)
- Goal: Validate production-like throughput and latency for Acme’s search API under peak QPS to size Dedicated capacity and validate fallback behavior.
- Target test window: proposed Sept 7–8 (will finalize after your confirmation)
- Test scope: 2 days of traffic replay (peak business hour windows), ramp to peak QPS and sustain for 30m intervals, end-to-end latencies + error rates, KV cache warm-up profile, and SLO verification.
- Acme responsibilities: provide traffic replay artifacts (sample traces, replay manifest, anonymized payloads), define peak QPS target and acceptable latency/error thresholds.
- Redwood responsibilities: provision dedicated capacity (GPU pool), prepare replay harness & routing, run tests, collect token-level latency/cost breakdowns, and deliver test report + recommendations for capacity and quantization if needed.
- Dependencies: access to a staging endpoint (read-only) or replay sandbox URL, sample data and manifests, and a point-of-contact for quick triage during the run.
- Decision / close criteria: capacity recommendation approved and a follow-up plan for production rollout or additional tuning.

Attached: initial MAP draft (ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx) and example replay manifest.

Next steps:
1) Tom/Jenna — confirm target peak QPS and whether the replay will run against the staging endpoint or a sandbox URL (reply by 08/31).
2) Redwood (Aditya/Vivek) — we'll size an initial Dedicated config once we have the QPS and sample payloads.
3) Schedule final test window & runbook once artifacts are in.

Let me know if you prefer a short 15-min sync to confirm the QPS and test windows.

Thanks Tom — good data. A few technical clarifications from the Redwood side so we can size correctly: 

1) Replay artifacts: please include example request/response pairs and an indication of payload size distribution. If there are any very large outliers (>1MB), call those out.
2) Traffic pattern: confirm whether peak QPS of 850 is sustained (steady-state) or bursty (e.g., 850 with frequent 1.2k spikes). We will model both but need the expected duration.
3) Cold vs warm: by default we'll perform a 20–30 minute warm-up run to populate KV cache and then run the sustained peak window. We'll also run a cold-start pass if you want separate results — let us know.
4) Staging endpoint access: we need an IP allowlist or a temporary token for the replay harness. If you prefer, we can spin up a sandbox endpoint in Redwood Private and replay there (requires ~48h lead time).

Initial sizing note (rough estimate): to support sustained 850 QPS with a 2–4k token average request and target P95 <300ms, we recommend starting with a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A100-class equivalent) with continuous batching and a KV cache layer. We'll finalize once we see sample payloads.

I can take point on the replay run — Marissa, I'll coordinate with Vivek to provision the pool and prepare the runbook once artifacts arrive.
